Personally, I like that mechanic. I wouldn't sat it's perfect the way it is, but I found I very rarely got a chance to use my rear focused attacks the way things were. Yeah. I didn't like how enemies would just scooch forward after you killed one of them to fill the gap. Corpses are an interesting idea, but have their own flaws... If an enemy is killed by by poison or bleed or critted, they don't leave a corpse, but do when they die normally? Whyyyyy?

My issue with the micro is the buying supplies for every run, which area has which intractables that need certain items to 'diffuse' them. Making a party that will work together every time and equip them with certain heirlooms... Gets a little tedious

they don't leave a corpse, but do when they die normally? Whyyyyy?

This was their (lazy) way of buffing the witch docker/disease-attacks, what was considered a weak class in early 2015. I think they cut too many corners and built too much hype up during open access. They shot themselves in the foot with their own success unfortunately. Should have developed it behind closed doors and given it the vision/direction it needed to be focused on being good, not focus on getting it done in time. They were under pressure to finish the game because it would appear that they were leading people along with another open access scam that never gets released.

My issue with the micro is the buying supplies for every run,

Now that I think about it, that was a problem too. It punished new players and rewarded players who have played the game many times. The problem the game had was that it was punishing new players too much, but letting min/max'ers (experienced players) cruise through. For example, I knew which supplies to buy not based on the description, but just experience with a particular area. They could have used more RNG there to prevent me from farming with min/max'ed supplies (eg: knowing almost exactly how many shovels to buy rewards experienced players too much and it's just an easymode farm game).

Agree on both points. They could have dropped hints or something... Anything... to prepare you for what you may encounter, for instance, in the weald. One of the heroes you select could say something like 'I could use that bandage on an old tree', well maybe not so obvious. You could even work it in as a quirk or something. Some heroes could lie about what they want on a journey. Come to think of it, why couldn't there be quirks for getting 10% off at the store or something, bartering. OK, getting off track. Personally, after getting my ass kicked on my first like 5 or 6 attempts, I just looked up what to bring where online. The curve is too steep in the beginning for the trial and error of wasting items on 'curios' or whatever.

Darkest Dungeon had so much potential and I really enjoyed it early on in it's development (i like a difficult game with amazing atmosphere to scratch my Demon's Souls itch).

But the devs seemed more interested in adding in unfun mechanics (see: corpses and heart attacks) than actual gameplay, IMO the game still starts out strong (even though I was losing heros left and right and desperately trying to not starve myself of resources) but it becomes an incredible grindfest in the midgame and you can lose hours of progress through no fault of your own (first room of long dungeon, ghoul dodges all of my attacks, critical howl adds 65 stress to entire party, end the fight with everyone nearly at a heartattack, forced to either abandon and lose all of the gold you spent on supplies + get even more stress or risk a TPK of my leveled heros to heartattacks).

Also screw the RNG hunger system.

In my mind the ideally difficult game is an extreme test of skill where you are expected to be the very best, like no one ever was and where no mistake goes unpunished not "the Ghoul crits your entire party, sending them all half way to death in a single turn, also go fuck yourself"
